strategies.overview: Arceus-Water is a solid defensive pick in Ubers, being one of the best answers to hard-to-check threats like Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM, Arceus-Ground, offensive Ho-Oh, Calyrex-I, Chien-Pao, Rayquaza, and Kyogre lacking Thunder. While it cannot compare to Arceus-Fairy in terms of taking on Koraidon, its resistance to Flare Blitz makes Arceus-Water a decent check in combination with other Koraidon switch-ins like Landorus-T. Arceus-Water can spread burns and paralysis with relative freedom, as it discourages Ground-types from switching in and the use of Tera Fire, not to mention that Calm Mind makes it a decent setup sweeper in combination with massive Defense investment. The most notable flaw of Arceus-Water is that it invites arguably the most threatening Pokemon in the tier, Miraidon, to come in with little risk; it is also quite passive and vulnerable to being worn down over time.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Dragon Dance sets are possible, but are too limited by Koraidon's sun and are generally outclassed by Extreme Killer Arceus and Arceus-Ground.

Checks and Counters

Miraidon: Miraidon can come in quite easily, as it can stomach an Ice Beam without much worry and blow past even a boosted Arceus-Water.

Poison: Eternatus and Clodsire can take even a boosted Ice Beam and immediately threaten Arceus-Water with Toxic, though they must be wary of Tera Poison. Specially defensive Gliscor is not OHKOed by Ice Beam or Judgment and thus can retaliate with Toxic. All of the aforementioned Pokemon can also set Toxic Spikes, which is devastating for Arceus-Water's longevity.

Kyogre: Kyogre can switch in without too much worry and use Thunder or Thunder Wave, both of which can cripple Arceus-Water. However, Kyogre will lose to Calm Mind sets if it lacks Thunder.

Arceus-Grass: Though rare, Arceus-Grass can boost alongside Arceus-Water and deal devastating damage at any time with Grass Knot.

Sun: Though Koraidon itself prefers to not be on the field when Arceus-Water is, the sun that it brings cripples the damage output that Arceus-Water would normally provide.

movesets.name: Defensive
movesets.description:
While Judgment has decent neutral coverage by itself, it's weakened by how common sun is, so a secondary attack is necessary. Ice Beam is usually chosen as the best option to hit switch-ins like Miraidon and Clodsire. Dragon Tail can rack up entry hazard damage and has good synergy with Arceus-Water's status options. Since Arceus-Water can often check most threats without status, Calm Mind is a great option to turn it into a solid win condition. Alternatively, Thunder Wave can cripple Ho-Oh and Tera Fire users like Koraidon, Necrozma-DM, and Calyrex-I, making it a safe option. Will-O-Wisp may be used to more solidly check physical threats. Do note that Tera Fire can put a stop to this, especially from Koraidon, which doesn't mind taking Judgment in the sun; therefore, Dragon Tail is highly recommended for Will-O-Wisp sets to mitigate this risk. Tera Fairy allows Arceus-Water to take boosted Scale Shot from Koraidon, while Tera Poison is possible on Calm Mind sets to prevent Arceus-Water from being crippled by Toxic from Eternatus, Clodsire, and specially defensive Gliscor. The EVs maximize Defense investment while outspeeding all neutral-natured base 90 Speed Pokemon.

Arceus-Water works best when it has other walls to back it up against powerful wallbreakers like Koraidon. Landorus-T has fantastic synergy with Arceus-Water, checking Pokemon like Zacian-C and Zekrom, and its Intimidate and Rocky Helmet support makes Koraidon much easier to handle. Necrozma-DM can check Zacian-C and Kyurem-B and appreciates Arceus-Water handling Calyrex-I. Ting-Lu is the most solid switch-in to Miraidon that often come in on Arceus-Water, making it a highly recommended teammate. Meanwhile, Clodsire can absorb Toxic Spikes and check Miraidon and Kyogre. Miraidon can help against Kyogre sets that have Thunder while also bringing in Arceus-Water easily with U-turn. Skeledirge likes Arceus-Water dealing with Ho-Oh and can handle Koraidon and Zacian-C for it in return. Flutter Mane is a good offensive partner that forces difficult decisions on opposing Koraidon as to what move to choose; using anything but Flare Blitz allows Flutter Mane in for free, while Flare Blitz allows Arceus-Water to switch in easily.

strategies.overview: Arceus-Water is one of the best physical walls in the metagame, being used on balance and bulky offense teams to check top threats like Necrozma-DM, Ho-Oh, and Koraidon with its great bulk, typing, and utility moves such as Will-O-Wisp and Dragon Tail. It can also be a decent wincon with Calm Mind, using its defensive profile to repeatedly set up and avoid revenge killing attempts. However, Pokemon like Miraidon and Eternatus can relatively freely switch into Arceus-Water and threaten it, the omnipresent Koraidon's sun weakens its Judgment, and it is vulnerable to being worn down into KO range of foes it's supposed to check by entry hazards.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Defensive Arceus-Water can use Calm Mind in the fourth moveslot to turn into a decent wincon, as it can use its bulk to set up on the foes it checks and avoid being revenge killed by Pokemon like Koraidon and Arceus. Draco Meteor is also an option in this moveslot to chip Koraidon, Miraidon, and Eternatus more reliably than Dragon Tail; Miriadon can only switch into it once, and it has a good chance to 2HKO Koraidon. Thunder Wave can be used over Will-O-Wisp to debilitate Calyrex-S, Eternatus, Ho-Oh, and Tera Fire users like Koraidon and Necrozma-DM, but this makes Arceus-Water worse against Arceus and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground.

Checks and Counters

Miriadon: Miraidon can switch into any of Arceus-Water's moves bar Dragon Tail with very little consequence to fire off its powerful attacks or grab momentum with U-turn.

Eternatus: Eternatus can repeatedly take Arceus-Water's moves and cripple it with Toxic or lay Toxic Spikes against it, though Tera Poison prevents this.

Calyrex-S: Calyrex-S can pretty safely switch into Arceus-Water, usually at worst taking a chunk from Judgment or being forced out by Dragon Tail, and use this as an opportunity to set up or immediately wallbreak. However, the rare Thunder Wave completely ruins Calyrex-S.

Kyogre: Kyogre is similarly able to use Arceus-Water as an entry point to use Calm Mind, Thunder, or Origin Pulse; it loses to Calm Mind Arceus-Water if it lacks Thunder, however.

Sun: Koraidon's sun severely weakens Arceus-Water's Judgment, making it struggle against foes like Ho-Oh, Ting-Lu, and Arceus-Ground or potentially impeding its sweep.

movesets.name: Defensive
movesets.description:
Arceus-Water is a good check to dangerous physical attackers like Necrozma-DM, Koraidon, Ho-Oh, Arceus, Arceus-Ground, and Zacian-C, and it soft checks non-Thunder Kyogre. Its resistances to moves like Necrozma-DM's Sunsteel Strike and Koraidon's Flare Blitz and—most importantly—its ability to beat Ho-Oh set it apart from its main competition in Arceus-Ground. Dragon Tail phazes setup sweepers like Necrozma-DM and Arceus formes, as well as chipping Pokemon such as Miraidon and Eternatus on the switch-in and racking up entry hazard damage. Alternatively, Taunt stops setup sweepers from boosting and Pokemon like Ting-Lu from laying entry hazards, and Stealth Rock greatly hinders Choice Band Ho-Oh and weakens defensive Pokemon for Arceus-Water's teammates. Tera Fairy lets Arceus-Water more comfortably take Koraidon's Low Kick and completely block its Scale Shot, denying it a Speed boost; Tera Fairy does make Arceus-Water weak to Necrozma-DM's Sunsteel Strike, however. Tera Poison also gives it a resistance to Low Kick, lets it absorb Toxic Spikes and Toxic from Eternatus, and improves its matchup against Wild Charge Zacian-C, albeit at the cost of leaving it vulnerable to foes like Necrozma-DM and Arceus-Ground. Both Tera types also help by removing Arceus-Water's weaknesses to Miraidon's Electro Drift and Calyrex-S's Grass Knot in a pinch.

Arceus-Water should be used on balance and bulky offense teams, where both offensive Pokemon and walls benefit from its defensive utility. Arceus-Water can switch into walls like Ho-Oh and Arceus-Ground and common revenge killers like Arceus and Choice Scarf Koraidon for offensive teammates such as Calyrex-S, Miraidon, Arceus, and Zacian-C. In return, Calyrex-S and Miraidon can threaten Eternatus, one of Arceus-Water's biggest problems, and Zacian-C can safely switch into Eternatus lacking a Fire-type move. Necrozma-DM appreciates Arceus-Water checking Koraidon and Arceus-Ground; additionally, Necrozma-DM helps handle Wild Charge Zacian-C, can take Choice Band Ho-Oh's Brave Bird—which 2HKOes Arceus-Water with entry hazards up—and is the best Eternatus check in the metagame. Ting-Lu can handle Calyrex-S, Miraidon, and, to a certain extent, Eternatus for Arceus-Water and appreciates it taking on Pokemon like Koraidon, Ho-Oh, and Zacian-C. Eternatus can check Kyogre and absorb Toxic Spikes for Arceus-Water, and Arceus-Water deals with Ground-types like Arceus-Ground and Ting-Lu. Ho-Oh likes that Arceus-Water checks Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground and some Kyogre and helps take on Pokemon like Koraidon and Arceus. Offensive Ho-Oh in particular can also potentially lure in and KO Eternatus.

movesets.name: Defensive
movesets.description: Arceus-Water differentiates itself from other bulky Water-types such as Mega Slowbro and Dondozo through its good Speed tier and balanced bulk, which makes it more resilient to slower wallbreakers like Mega Garchomp. Its Special Defense also means it doesn't instantly fold to Electro Drift coverage, while the aforementioned Water-types are both OHKOed by any Tough Claws user with it. Fur Coat allows Arceus-Water to wall threats like Mega Garchomp and Ash-Greninja, albeit needing a Bold nature to dodge a potential 2HKO from Ash-Greninja's Flower Trick. Scald threatens burns on Pokemon like Mega Lucario and defensive switch-ins like RegenVest users. Due to Arceus-Water's weakness to Thunder Cage, Spirit Shackle is the safest option for Fur Coat variants to Imposter-proof themselves. Spirit Shackle variants can utilize Shore Up to not have recovery denied by Magic Guard Blissey. Arceus-Water still takes a lot of damage from coverage options like Electro Drift and Ash-Greninja's Flower Trick, so backup checks to these like Dragon-types and Fur Coat Fairy-types help. Arceus-Water can generally Imposter-proof itself but can always be Imposter-proofed by Imposter Chansey as a backup.

movesets.name: Defensive
movesets.description: Arceus-Water is an excellent physical wall, capable of switching into powerful physical attackers such as Great Tusk, Hisuian Arcanine, and Entei. It has access to valuable utility moves like Will-O-Wisp, which can cripple strong physical threats such as Urshifu-R, and Calm Mind, which provides Arceus-Water a modest offensive presence, especially when it is using Judgment as its only damage-dealing move. Ice Beam provides crucial coverage against the likes of Eternatus, Zapdos, and Raging Bolt, which can otherwise check Arceus-Water. Although somewhat niche, it can also run other utility options such as Stealth Rock and Thunder Wave; however, if reflected by Magic Bounce users, these moves can result in significant momentum loss or heavily debilitate Arceus-Water by setting entry hazards on its side or paralyzing it. The Speed EVs allow Arceus-Water to outspeed Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk. Arceus-Water fits exceptionally well on bulky offense and balance archetypes. Pairing it with specially defensive partners like Magearna, Garganacl, Mandibuzz, and Ho-Oh helps form a robust defensive core capable of handling a large portion of the metagame. Arceus-Water dislikes switching into hazards, as multiple threats, such as Urshifu-R, can then 2HKO it as well as force it to use Recover more often. Therefore, hazard control from teammates such as Regieleki, Great Tusk, Mandibuzz, and Corviknight is crucial to maintain Arceus-Water's longevity. Electric-types like Raging Bolt and Zapdos are among the best checks to Arceus-Water, particularly if they avoid taking an Ice Beam on the switch or when it isn't using the move at all. Electric-resistant and Electric-immune Pokemon like Dragonite, Eternatus, Clodsire, and Hippowdon are excellent choices to cover that weakness. Despite being able to comfortably switch into Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes, Arceus-Water struggles to check it long term, particularly if Urshifu-R is carrying Close Combat. As such, sturdier answers like Pecharunt and Rocky Helmet Eternatus make great partners, as they can reliably answer Urshifu-R.

movesets.name: Defensive Calm Mind
movesets.description:
• Arceus-Water's excellent typing, supplemented by superb natural bulk, is attractive to balance teams looking for a sweeper that also contributes defensively as a switch-in to specially offensive Yveltal, a Pokemon balance teams lacking Arceus-Fairy notoriously struggle with, while also scaring out Ho-Oh.
  • As Judgment, Calm Mind, and Recover are all mandatory, Arceus-Water only has one moveslot left for coverage. Unfortunately, there is no singular move that perfectly complements Judgment, leaving Arceus-Water reliant on teammates to handle certain Pokemon it does not have coverage for. Ice Beam enables Arceus-Water to hit Pokemon that would otherwise wall it such as Mega Salamence, Rayquaza, and Giratina-O while ensuring Primal Groudon does not switch in freely. Alternatively, Earth Power heavily punishes Primal Groudon attempting to freely switch in on Judgment while preventing Arceus-Water from being walled by Water-types such as Primal Kyogre and opposing Arceus-Water.
  • The given EV spread ensures that Arceus-Water outspeeds fully invested neutral-natured base 90 Speed Pokemon such as Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre. Furthermore, the high investment in bulk enables Arceus-Water to survive some monstrously powerful attacks including Basculegion's Last Respects after five fainted allies, +3 Zacian-C's Wild Charge, Deoxys-A's Psycho Boost after Stealth Rock, and Tera Flying Choice Band Rayquaza's Dragon Ascent after Stealth Rock and a single layer of Spikes. Additionally, Arceus-Water avoids the 2HKO from Double Dance Primal Groudon's Precipice Blades and Choice Band Marshadow's Low Kick.
  • Though Arceus-Water rarely Terastallizes, it can still effectively utilize its Tera type in a pinch to help flip certain matchups or to facilitate a sweep. Tera Fairy transforms Arceus-Water from a passable to sturdy specially offensive Yveltal check while retaining a stellar defensive typing and becoming a good Marshadow check. Tera Poison is an alternate option that enables Arceus-Water to more consistently sweep bulkier balance teams. The newfound Toxic immunity enables Arceus-Water to switch into Ho-Oh and defensive Eternatus with impunity and use them as setup fodder. Absorbing Eternatus's Toxic Spikes has the added benefit of alleviating pressure on teammates to use Defog. However, Arceus-Water's new weakness to the omnipresent Ground-type attacks from Primal Groudon and Arceus-Ground means that Tera Poison should be used cautiously.
  • Arceus-Water excels against balance and bulky offense teams. It has a strong mid-game presence, as it prevents Ho-Oh, defensive Yveltal, and—if Arceus-Water runs Ice Beam—Giratina-O from freely removing entry hazards. However, Arceus-Water should do so cautiously, as all three commonly run Toxic, which can prevent Arceus-Water from sweeping in the end-game. Arceus-Water lacks the ability to make progress against stall teams and is overwhelmed by hyper offense teams due to a lack of power before boosting.
  • As Arceus-Water has coverage issues regardless of whether it runs Ice Beam or Earth Power, it relies on teammates to fill these gaps. Zygarde is an excellent choice as a blanket physical wall that checks Pokemon such as Primal Groudon, Rayquaza, and Mega Salamence. Zygarde also alleviates pressure on Arceus-Water defensively, which enables it to more consistently sweep. In return, Arceus-Water checks Taunt Arceus-Ground and specially offensive Yveltal, which shut down Zygarde. Ferrothorn is also an excellent teammate due to checking wallbreaker Primal Kyogre, which can easily run through many balance teams, especially if a Timid nature is used. Arceus-Water also appreciates offensive partners such as Choice Band Marshadow and specially offensive Yveltal, which thrive against the hyper offense and stall teams that Arceus-Water struggles with due to their ability to revenge kill Pokemon such as Zacian-C, Mega Salamence, and Ultra Necrozma.

movesets.name: Offensive Calm Mind
movesets.description:
• With access to Calm Mind and excellent base 120 stats across the board, Arceus-Water is able to act as a strong bulky setup sweeper.
  • Arceus-Water's good typing allows it to break through defensive staples such as Ho-Oh and Arceus-Ground while dealing great damage to Zygarde.
  • Calm Mind allows Arceus-Water to 2HKO walls like Necrozma-DM and Primal Groudon. Aside from boosting Arceus-Water's Special Attack, it also allows it to turn the tables on some switch-ins that typically check it such as Eternatus and Palkia-O; in conjunction with Recover, it provides Arceus-Water with the longevity needed to continuously take on strong special attacks from foes like Eternatus and offensive Yveltal in order to set up on them.
  • Earth Power enables Arceus-Water to threaten foes that can take Water-type moves, 2HKOing Primal Groudon and Eternatus at +1. Grass Knot can also be used instead of Earth Power to hit heavy Water-types like Primal Kyogre, Palkia-O, and opposing Arceus-Water.
  • Arceus-Water's choice of Tera type is determined by the coverage move it runs. Tera Ground boosts Earth Power to muscle through Primal Groudon and Zacian-C with an OHKO on both at +1 whilst granting it an immunity to Electric-type attacks from Zekrom and Primal Kyogre. Tera Grass is used to power up Grass Knot, and at +1 it has a chance to OHKO Primal Kyogre and deal significant damage to Zygarde whilst resisting its Ground-type STAB moves and the aforementioned Electric-type Arceus-Water best fits on bulky and hyper offense teams that appreciate its great bulk and typing.
  • It is preferable to use Arceus-Water early-game to blow holes into the opposing team's defensive core, as it can easily use Calm Mind on the likes of Ho-Oh and Zygarde and force progress, which is appreciated by teammates such as Necrozma-DM and offensive Primal Groudon. It also has good synergy with the aforementioned teammates, as it helps them beat physical walls like Zygarde and opposing Primal Groudon.
  • Although Arceus-Water has good Special Attack, it struggles to beat special walls such as Chansey, Ferrothorn, and Giratina, so teammates like Primal Groudon, Marshadow, and Zacian-C are appreciated.
  • Fairy-types like Zacian-C help Arceus-Water deal with Dragon-type foes, as it struggles to deal damage to foes such as Ultra Necrozma, Mega Salamence, and Rayquaza. In return, Arceus-Water can beat foes such as Primal Groudon and Ho-Oh for them.

movesets.name: Calm Mind + Refresh
movesets.description:
• Calm Mind Arceus-Water is already a potent sweeper by itself, and with the addition of Refresh, it can be almost impossible to stop once it gets going, beating traditional checks like Giratina-O and Eternatus. The one caveat of this set is its inability to hit Primal Groudon at all, requiring the team to be built around hitting it with Toxic or easily removing it. Furthermore, this set does not forgo Arceus-Water’s defensive utility, as it still checks Necrozma-DM and Ho-Oh, and the set even expands on its utility with the addition of Refresh enabling it to become a status absorber.
  • Calm Mind functions both as a defensive tool and an offensive one, letting Arceus-Water actually pressure Zygarde and Eternatus while also setting itself up for a sweep late-game.
  • Refresh lets Arceus-Water shrug off Toxic from Ho-Oh and Eternatus, utilizing them as setup fodder, and freely pivot into Necrozma-DM without worrying about being statused.
  • The given EV spread with a Timid nature lets Arceus-Water outspeed Modest Palkia-O and offensive Yveltal, allowing it to use Calm Mind or Recover before it can throw off an attack, with the remainder of the EVs dumped in Defense to maximize its defensive utility; this notably lets it avoid the KO from +2 Searing Sunraze Smash from Necrozma-DM after Stealth Rock and +1 Tectonic Rage from Arceus Ground.
  • Tera Fairy gives Arceus-Water a better defensive typing that prevents it from being phazed by Dragon Tail Zygarde and Giratina-O, lets it swtch into non-Sludge Bomb Eternatus better, and prevents it from being forced out by non-Behemoth Blade Zacian-C. As Arceus-Water doesn't require Terastallizing often to sweep, Tera Fairy is mainly used to enhance its defensive role if it is unable to sweep, letting it check Life Orb Yveltal and Marshadow better.
  • Calm Mind + Refresh Arceus-Water should always be paired with a teammate that can either lure or put immense pressure on Primal Groudon. Arceus-Water is best used mid- or late-game, as its defensive utility allows it to stave off threats like Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM and Palkia O, and it can sweep once Primal Groudon is poisoned or removed. If Primal Groudon cannot be removed or hit by Toxic easily, then Arceus-Water can be relegated to a more defensive role throughout the match and absorb status for its teammates safely; in a pinch, it can Tera to check a wider array of threats. Shuca Berry Eternatus is the most notable example, as it lures in Primal Groudon and poisons it, essentially allowing Arceus-Water to set up on it freely and win. Primal Kyogre is also a great partner, as it constantly forces in and pressures Primal Groudon and Eternatus, which can heavily annoy Arceus-Water. Zacian-C functions similarly to wear down Primal Groudon throughout a game or even outright remove it with Tera Blast Ground.
  • Gothitelle is also a notable partner that can trap and remove defensive Primal Groudon lacking Overheat, but it struggles against offensive variants and defensive ones with Overheat. As such, additional support is needed alongside it, such as Toxic Spikes or Dragonium Z Eternatus. Zygarde is also great alongside Arceus-Water, as it checks Primal Groudon consistently while also appreciating Arceus-Water checking Kyogre and offensive Yveltal for it.
